children: , the enterprise-software and cloud-infrastructure company, rose approximately 4.9% to $142.405 as of approximately 11:17 a.m. ET Friday, October 9, with a $3.48 million insider purchase adding a confidence signal. Director Stephen Rusckowski put substantial money behind the business. According to Barron's reporting, this was his first open-market purchase since joining the board.

The SEC filing records a September 29 purchase of 25,000 shares through Rusckowski's trust at a weighted-average price of $139.352, lifting his reported holdings to 25,390 shares. Shares now sit roughly 2.2% above that entry point. The picture shows a 26.94% discount to the $194.91 GF Value estimate, suggesting valuation headroom if Oracle delivers on its growth ambitions.

An insider's check gets attention. Cash generation earns conviction. Oracle still needs its AI-cloud commitments to translate into busy data centers, healthy margins and stronger free cash flow. Rusckowski's purchase supports the confidence case, but it cannot settle the execution question: how much cash will remain after Oracle pays to build the infrastructure behind those contracts?

title: Oracle Stocks Jump 4.9% as Insider Risks $3.5 Million
